$comment: MONEY MODULE (pack: orders) — shaped to bizapps-orders' published design: one renewal Order per membership cycle (BO-D40/D45 — the posted Order IS the bill; no invoices), product-typed lines, and payment timing per the GAP-1-approved 3-part mixture (Atradius/CRF primary sources).

paymentProfiles.$note: DECLARED derivedTransaction timing grammar (core/patterns.mjs) — the GAP-1-approved 3-part mixture, now authored here instead of coded in money.mjs. Each profile: method (fixed) or methods (uniform pick), lateShare (bernoulli branch), and late/onTime day-offset distributions relative to the due date. Same numbers as the previous paymentTiming block; byte-identical migration.

netTerms.$evidence: Atradius/CRF B2B late curve: ~45% late, log-normal ~12d median, thin tail capped

autopay.$note: auto-pay lands ON the due date; the lateShare is the failed-card retry tail

manual.$note: manual individual dues spread early-to-grace; lateShare mirrors late_renewal_share 0.25

checkout.$note: event registrations: card at checkout, same day

paymentOutcomes.$note: payment lifecycle enrichment (feedback 2026-07-16). DELIBERATE causal-vs-noise mix: a base failure rate that is pure noise + an affluence-driven component (low-phi members' cards fail more) — so 'find what is causal' is an honest analyst exercise with a known answer. Failed attempts precede the retry; a retry landing after release leaves the order OVERDUE (the failed card IS the churn-adjacent story). In-flight payments near release sit InProgress.
paymentOutcomes.$noiseFailSource: SOURCED 2026-07-16 (confidence: high): this models ULTIMATE unrecovered card failure after retries, not per-attempt declines. SaaS involuntary churn ~0.86%/month (churnkey.co involuntary-churn-benchmarks); per-attempt declines run far higher (Recurly: 5-14% of monthly subscription transactions, credit cards averaging 7.6% - blog.recurly.com benchmarking-decline-rates). 1.5% +/-0.5 final-failure is well supported.

orders.$revenueNote: The federation used to sell exactly two things. Certifications and competition entries — real billable facts already in the data — generated NO revenue at all, every order had exactly one line of quantity one, and prices had not moved in thirteen years, so a revenue-by-year chart was pure volume with no price effect. Catalogue prices below are CURRENT (release-year); an order line is charged the price of ITS year via priceIndex, which is how a historical order actually reads.

priceIndex.$note: ESTIMATE (confidence: medium) — long-run consumer inflation over the simulated window, applied so an order line carries the price of its own year. Rounded to whole currency units, as a real price list is.

certificationFees.$note: every credential pursuit is billed an exam fee; most renewals of an expiring credential are billed a recertification fee

competitionFees.$note: every entry pays an entry fee — this is how competitions fund themselves

addOns.$note: multi-line orders: conference registrations often pick up merchandise, and some dues renewals add the journal or a donation. Fixes the strict 1 order = 1 line shape.

refunds.$note: a share of paid no-shows are actually refunded — Payment.Status already permits 'Refunded', so this needs no schema change. The refund is a NEGATIVE payment against the original order, which is how an AMS records it.
